Non-depolarising neuromuscular blockers (ND-NMBs) are competitive antagonists of the nicotinic ACh receptor at the neuromuscular junction

Rate of recovery depends on:

(1) concentration of ND-NMB at the NMJ
(2) pharmacokinetic factors
(3) pharmacodynamic factors – either drug or patient factors

**Concentration of ND-NMB at the NMJ**

As per Fick’s law of diffusion, Increasing dose of rocuronium →↑Rocuronium at NMJ →↑time for diffusion back into plasma →↑duration of block 

Time since administration →↓time since administration →↑ plasma/NMJ Concentration →↑time till recovery 

**Pharmacokinetic factors**

Distribution:

↑Vd →↑recovery after single bolus (because ↑redistribution) 

↑Vd →↓recovery after infusion (because more accumulation)

Metabolism:

Hepatic disease →↓biliary excretion →↓rate of recovery 

↓non-specific plasma esterase →↓metabolism of atracurium →↓rate of recovery 

Excretion:

Renal disease →↓renal excretion →↓rate of recovery

**Pharmacodynamic Factors:**

**Patient factors** that slow rate of recovery

(1) acidosis → slower metabolism
(2) hypothermia → slower metabolism
(3) hypocalcaemia →↓pre-synaptic ACh release at NMJ
(4) hypokalaemia → hyperpolarise post-synaptic membrane
(5) hypermagnesemia →  competes with Ca2+ →↓pre-synaptic ACh release 
(6) NMJ disorders: e.g. myasthenia gravis, burns, spinal cord injury
(7) Neonatal →↑sensitivity to NMD → prolonged action

**Drug factors** that slow rate of recovery

(1) volatile anaesthetics → via multiple mechanisms: central motor neuron inhibition, increase affinity of nAChR for NMBs, direct depression of post-synaptic nAChR (at high MAC)
(2) aminoglycoside antibiotics →↓presynaptic ACh release 
(3) local anaesthetics (high doses) → stabilise post-synaptic membrane and direct muscle fibre depression
(4) calcium channel blockers →↓ACh release
(5) frusemide →↓ACh release + causes hypokalaemia

::: {}
(7) magnesium →↓ACh release (esp. with vecuronium)
:::

Drug factors that increase rate of recovery

1.  anticholinesterase!↑\[ACh\] at NMJ
2.  Gamma Cyclodextrin (sugammadex) → forms complex with rocuronium in plasma → concentration gradient to remove roc from NMJ
